output.question:
A closed cylindrical container has an interior radius of 6 centimeters and an interior height of 15 centimeters. A solid sphere with a radius of 3 centimeters is placed inside the container, and the rest of the container is completely filled with water. What is the volume, in cubic centimeters, of the water in the container?
Answer choices: A) 468pi, B) 504pi, C) 540pi, D) 576pi
output.structure: cylinder volume minus sphere volume (use volume formulas)

result.detail: volume divided by \pi (cubic cm per \pi)
(cylinder vol - sphere vol) divided by \pi
the second list entry equals the computed volume/\pi
Cylinder: \pi(6^2)(15)=540\pi; sphere: \frac{4}{3}\pi(3^3)=36\pi; difference=504\pi
